runners_data.name: Apple's Angel
runners_data.note: A 4yo filly for Jim Boyle whose recent form reads 7-9846 at 6f on Good, suggesting she struggles to land a blow even at a shorter trip; her natural style is a deep hold-up run that will leave her buried in traffic here, and 30 days since her last start adds a mild freshness question — the 7f step up is untested in her recent record.

runners_data.name: Barnsnape Boy
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's 5yo has placed three times in his last five over 7f on Good and is the most interesting hold-up type in this field given that experience; naturally a rear-of-field operator, he is one of several pushed onto the pace map in midfield, but his Good-ground 7f form (including a win) gives him the strongest profile of the chasing pack if he can break smartly and secure a position closer than natural.

runners_data.name: Port Hedland
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's 5yo goes on Good ground and won over 6f on Good in recent form, and with no confirmed front runner to oppose him he finds himself redistributed to the lead as the most likely pace-setter; he is a genuine prominent type rather than a natural leader, so the question is whether he has the tactical cruising speed to maintain a controlled solo lead over 7f — his 1-win record at the distance in good ground conditions is the key qualifier.

runners_data.name: River Wharfe
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran for Tony Carroll who won over 8f on Good and has headgear noted; last ran just one day ago which is an obvious concern for residual fatigue, and while his preferred trip appears to be a mile rather than this 7f, his ability to track pace from a natural hold-up position could see him make the frame if Port Hedland is caught early.

runners_data.name: Rock Master
runners_data.note: Carroll's 4yo has a form string of 988066 and has been beaten out of the placings in every recent start over 7-8f; habitually races from a hold-up position and is shown in midfield on the map having been pushed forward — his poor recent form and lowest OR in the field (41) make him the most difficult to support.

runners_data.name: Spirited Dancer
runners_data.note: The Kubler-trained 4yo showed clear ability when placed twice at 6f on Good and once over 7f on Good, and only six days since his last start suggests peak fitness; naturally a hold-up type who will be squeezed into midfield alongside several rivals, but his consistent form at this distance and going gives him a legitimate chance if he can find a clear run — the small jockey claim could be useful in a congested finish.

runners_data.name: Valadero
runners_data.note: Brian Toomey's 5yo placed over 6f on Good in his most recent British turf form but has been beaten consistently on Tapeta since; 41 days since last run raises a fitness angle, and while his best-form going is this Good-to-Firm surface, he is a natural hold-up horse who wears blinkers and will face the same traffic issues as the majority of this field.

runners_data.name: Voodoo Ray
runners_data.note: Gary & Josh Moore's 7yo veteran has gone 49 days since his last run and has not won in his last five outings; blinkers are noted, and while he has placed at 6f on Good, his form on comparable going at 7f is limited — he represents the combination of a long absence, modest recent form and a compressed field position that makes him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Port Hedland is the lone confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the lead having been identified as the most likely pace-maker from a field that is overwhelmingly hold-up in nature, and with just one horse likely to press forward the tempo figures to be controlled and sustainable rather than pressured. The seven remaining runners — Apple's Angel, Barnsnape Boy, Rock Master, Spirited Dancer, Valadero, Voodoo Ray and River Wharfe — are all genuine hold-up or rear-of-field types who will be competing for space in the midfield-to-rear division, leaving Port Hedland alone on the bridle across Brighton's undulating 7f. This race shape strongly favours a horse capable of tracking the pace from just off it in the first two or three positions, as Port Hedland sets a gentle tempo with no pressure and the closers face a traffic-management problem having been compressed into a tight bunch. Several runners are redistributed on the pace map — Valadero, Spirited Dancer, Barnsnape Boy and others are natural hold-up horses shown in midfield because the map cannot place all of them at the rear — and only one or two of those will actually secure a genuinely forward tactical position; the remainder will be unable to race where they want and that compression in the chasing pack is the defining tactical feature of this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Port Hedland Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Port Hedland is allowed to stride clear on a gentle gallop and none of the hold-up pack can organise a sustained challenge from deep.
scenarios.body: Port Hedland controls every yard from the front without a rival willing or able to close the gap early on Good to Firm ground, and the lone pace-setter is never headed; horses who naturally track the leader in the first three are best placed here, but with nobody tracking closely, the race becomes Port Hedland's to lose.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one horse — most likely Barnsnape Boy or Spirited Dancer — manages to break quickly and tuck into second or third behind Port Hedland, giving them a clear sightline to strike.
scenarios.body: A horse that secures the coveted tracking position two or three lengths off the lone leader gets a clean run and a clear sprint finish, avoiding the compressed bunch behind; on good-to-firm Brighton, where momentum and forward position matter enormously on the false-flat finish, that horse hits the line with energy to spare.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Navigate Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If Port Hedland sets a genuinely fast early pace that brings the field to them and creates gaps through the compressed midfield bunch in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up horse that finds daylight late — Valadero or Barnsnape Boy using their natural finishing style — could pick off tired rivals if the tempo has been hot enough to bring Port Hedland back; this is the least straightforward scenario given how tightly packed the hold-up contingent will be.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Blanket Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Port Hedland fades sharply after setting a moderate pace and the entire field converges simultaneously in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With all eight runners arriving in a heap, the race devolves into a sprint for the line from the two-pole; the most recent form, freshest horse and best finishing kick on the day wins, making this almost unpredictable — but a horse with a clean passage and sharp acceleration such as Spirited Dancer could benefit.

watchPoints.text: River Wharfe ran just one day ago — monitor for signs of fatigue or sluggish early movement at the start, as a horse running on consecutive days over a trip shorter than preferred can be a drifting liability in running.

Port Hedland's solo lead could become a gift if he is allowed to set a crawl — watch whether any rider attempts to push up alongside him early, as even one horse pressing him could transform the race shape entirely.

Barnsnape Boy and Spirited Dancer will both attempt to break quickly and secure the same forward tracking position; if they collide for that berth at the top of the straight, both could lose momentum at a critical point.

The entire hold-up contingent — six horses — will be racing in a compressed bunch through the middle of the race; watch for signs of traffic interference and interference complaints in the stewards' room, particularly in the final 2f as the field fans across Brighton's finish.

Good to Firm conditions reported throughout the card — watch the going underfoot in the 2:38 slot if there has been any late watering update, as this could alter the relative merits of horses whose form is specifically on Good versus Good to Firm.

runners_data.name: Dandy G Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer trained by Warren Greatrex who won over 7f at Salisbury on fast ground recently but has otherwise been inconsistent, recording two sixes in recent starts; distance looks fine but the strongest form is on artificial surfaces and similar-going stats show no wins and no places in 15 comparable runs, which is a concern at this level.

runners_data.name: Boubyan
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old drops from 10f back to the mile trip on which he ran a decent second last time out; a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in the front-runner, and Kaiya Fraser must deliver a well-timed run from the rear to threaten on ground that has been kind to him statistically (two places in 15 similar-going runs).

runners_data.name: Gone Rogue
runners_data.note: Tom Queally takes the ride on Gary & Moore's five-year-old who arrives as a genuine hold-up horse with the most productive recent form in the field, winning last time over 10f on Good and placing four times in 15 similar-going starts; the drop in trip from 10f to 8f is a minor query, but the horse has proven over 8f before and is the strongest closer in the field.

runners_data.name: Danehill Star
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old is the lone front-runner and the architect of the entire race shape; William Carson can dictate from the front on Good to Firm ground, and while the horse has no wins in 15 similar-going runs, six places suggests he handles the conditions and the lack of pace pressure is a significant tactical advantage over his OR of 61.

runners_data.name: Kondratiev Wave
runners_data.note: The nine-year-old Carroll runner has prominent tendencies and two places in eight similar-going starts, though the veteran's flat recent form (422462) suggests his best days may be behind him; Jack Doughty will slot in just behind stablemate Danehill Star, making this a potentially team-handed scenario, though the horse's age and declining profile temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Winemaker
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse whose recent form includes a win over 6f on Flat at Sandown, though all recent starts have been on artificial surfaces and the step up to turf over a mile is uncharted territory; racing closer to the pace than is natural for this horse due to redistribution, and the style compromise — combined with limited turf-mile evidence — makes it difficult to assess with confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Danehill Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, William Carson can control the tempo from the outset over Brighton's undulating mile. Kondratiev Wave will press forward into a prominent position just off the leader, and Dandy G Boy is also a prominent-type who will look to sit close to the pace — meaning the first three positions are effectively occupied by horses with forward intentions. Both Boubyan and Gone Rogue are genuine hold-up horses who will settle in behind and rely on a sustained gallop to bring their late efforts into play, while Winemaker — a true hold-up type — has been mapped to midfield because the rear positions are already occupied by two classier closers and the field holds more genuine hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the back. The field holds more hold-up horses than can all settle in their natural position off the pace, with Boubyan and Gone Rogue most likely to secure the rear berths ahead of Winemaker. With Danehill Star able to dictate an uncontested, honest but not frantic gallop on Good to Firm ground, this race shape most favours prominent racers who can track the leader without burning fuel, as the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to reel in a leader setting a sustainable fractions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Danehill Star Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Danehill Star leads at a sustainable gallop and denies rivals a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: William Carson sets a controlled tempo that suits his horse's front-running profile, and the lack of a genuine pace rival means Danehill Star conserves energy through the early stages and has enough in reserve to repel challengers in the final furlong. Prominent trackers who can maintain contact over the final two furlongs are best placed to pick up any scraps, as the steady gallop will blunt the effectiveness of hold-up finishes.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to unwind Danehill Star in the final furlong, allowing a prominent racer to sweep past.
scenarios.body: Kondratiev Wave or Dandy G Boy, travelling smoothly just off the shoulder of the leader, inherit the advantage as Danehill Star ties up close home after setting fractions on quick going. This shape suits horses who have been saving ground while maintaining contact rather than those making up substantial distances from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong, stretching the field and leaving the door ajar for hold-up horses in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Gone Rogue, winner last time and carrying strong recent form with six placings in 15 similar-ground runs, is the likeliest beneficiary if a strong pace finally delivers a proper test that suits finishers. Boubyan has place claims in this shape too, having placed twice in 15 similar-going starts, though both horses need more pace than Danehill Star is likely to inject.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If the early order breaks down or Danehill Star is taken on unexpectedly, creating an uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: An erratic tempo would muddle the race shape, removing any particular style advantage and opening the result to chance, though horses with class at the top of the weights — Dandy G Boy and Boubyan — may pick up the pieces. Winemaker, a true hold-up horse racing out of its natural position here, would not benefit from a messy shape despite being mapped closer to the action.

watchPoints.text: Watch Danehill Star's early stride — if William Carson is allowed to bowl along uncontested at halfway, he may prove very difficult to catch from the front over a mile on Good to Firm at Brighton.

Winemaker's true hold-up style is being compromised by a crowded rear, meaning it may not get the ground-saving run it needs; if it does find space wide and late, it remains a minor threat under Richard Hughes.

The two Tony Carroll runners (Danehill Star and Kondratiev Wave) create a potential team dynamic — monitor whether Kondratiev Wave is used to control the tempo on behalf of the lead horse or is allowed to race on merit.

Gone Rogue arrives in the best recent form of the closers, but Tom Queally will need a genuine pace to work with; if Danehill Star crawls, Gone Rogue's strong finishing effort over 8f may not fire in time.

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this race despite the Flat card headline showing Good — on proper fast ground Brighton's undulations favour horses who travel fluently in the first half of the race rather than those making up ground from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Bohemian Breeze
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over shorter trips (10f) hint at reserve stamina that may fully emerge at this 14f trip; Warren Fentiman's 3lb claim is a practical benefit and the hold-up style suits a contested-pace scenario, though Brighton's undulations at this distance are a mild concern first time at the trip.

runners_data.name: Tai Hang Pegasus
runners_data.note: Front-runner for Charlie Fellowes whose 14-day strike rate of 0 from 12 is a negative angle; the horse has placed three times at 12f on Good but has never won, and being drawn into an early battle with Nibras Gold risks both horses' finishing chances — the pace contest may ultimately serve others more than it serves Tai Hang Pegasus.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus are both confirmed front-runners, meaning the early stages of this 1m4f Brighton contest will feature a genuine battle for lead position, most likely producing an honest, sustained gallop rather than a dawdle. Nibras Gold has strong course-and-distance form and has won over 12f on Good ground, making him the more credible pace-setter; Tai Hang Pegasus has finished placed at this trip but has not yet won, and may find the older, more experienced Nibras Gold dictating terms. Sarangpur and Brave Hunter sit prominently behind, meaning there is little cover for hold-up horses Maasai Mara and Bohemian Breeze, who will be forced to travel wider and later than ideal. With two pace-setters ensuring genuine early fractions on Good to Firm ground over a stamina-testing distance, this race shape favours closers and hold-up types who can conserve energy early and pick up off the pace — but only if the front-runners are genuinely run into the ground; if the gallop regulates, the prominent racers Sarangpur and Brave Hunter are ideally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runners Battle, Fade
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus push each other along at a genuine clip, setting up the race for those who settle off the pace.
scenarios.body: The contested early lead draws both pace-setters into an attritional duel that leaves them vulnerable from two furlongs out, gifting Sarangpur and Bohemian Breeze the ideal delivery. Sarangpur's recent winning form over this trip on Good ground and Bohemian Breeze's back-to-back wins suit horses who can pick up in the final quarter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Nibras Gold Dictates Alone
scenarios.trigger: If Tai Hang Pegasus misses the break or settles back, allowing Nibras Gold to find an uncontested lead and control fractions.
scenarios.body: Nibras Gold, an 8-year-old with three wins from his last eight starts at similar good-ground trips, thrives when able to dictate a measured tempo rather than scrap for every yard. From an uncontested front, he can balance through the race and potentially hold on under Pat Dobbs, whose track record here helps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly searching and front-runners tie up inside the final furlong, allowing deep hold-up runners to arrive with a late swoop.
scenarios.body: Maasai Mara and Bohemian Breeze, both running from off the pace, would benefit from maximum attrition at the front — Bohemian Breeze's recent form (two consecutive wins) makes her the more credible of the two to close late. Maasai Mara's poor recent win-rate and 55-day absence temper confidence, though William Carson is adept at timing late challenges.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace settles quickly after a brief skirmish and Sarangpur and Brave Hunter travel prominently without over-exerting themselves.
scenarios.body: In a scenario where fractions are honest but not excessive, Sarangpur's in-form profile (four wins from last six) and Brave Hunter's consistent placing on Good ground keep them dangerous throughout. Brave Hunter's higher OR of 80 offers a class edge but he has yet to win a handicap, so Sarangpur remains the more reliable beneficiary of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Gold and Tai Hang Pegasus are on a collision course for the early lead — if neither backs down, watch for both to show signs of distress entering the final two furlongs, which would sharply elevate the chances of Sarangpur and Bohemian Breeze.

Bohemian Breeze has won twice recently but both victories came over 10f; this is her first attempt at 14f and if the trip stretches her stamina, her late run may simply not materialise in the closing stages.

Maasai Mara is 55 days off the track with a trainer showing 0 from 2 over the past fortnight — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness in the early stages, as his hold-up style already requires a perfect trip.

Brave Hunter's visor was fitted for his last run (finished 5th on Good over 12f) — watch whether the headgear sharpens his early engagement or causes him to race too keenly in a prominent position over this longer trip.

Going confirmation is Good to Firm rather than the Good listed — all six runners are marked OK for the going, but the faster surface will quicken the pace further and may compress the finishing window, compressing the advantage of hold-up horses like Maasai Mara.

races.paceDynamic: Gearing's Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated tempo over 1m4f on Good to Firm ground at Brighton. Dream Of Ithaca is the only other horse with prominent tendencies, but has shown nothing in recent form to suggest she will press Gearing's Point hard, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than scorching — controlled by one horse setting its own rhythm. The hold-up trio of Alex The Great, Dogged, and Foinix sit at the back of a small field, with Lady Lauren also naturally suited to coming from behind, but the redistribution note highlights that several of these will be forced closer than ideal given the limited runners and the modest pace being set. This race shape overwhelmingly favours the horse who leads and controls — a front-runner dictating an uncontested, metronomic gallop over a flat mile-and-four is the dominant tactical picture, with hold-up horses facing the double jeopardy of a small field and a pace that may not set them alight late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gearing's Point Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gearing's Point leads unchallenged and sets a measured pace that suits a winner from the front.
scenarios.body: Gearing's Point, which won over 12f on Good ground in its recent history, bowls along uncontested and times the race to perfection, never coming off the bridle until asked in the straight; on Good to Firm ground at Brighton over 1m4f, a relaxed leader who has won at this course and distance profile holds all the trump cards in a small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If Gearing's Point sets a genuinely strong pace that strings the field out and the hold-up horses find enough late momentum.
scenarios.body: Dogged or Foinix, coming from the rear of a small group, peg back a tiring leader in the final furlong if the early gallop proves more taxing than expected; both carry headgear and have placed form on Good ground, making them the most credible late threats from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out

scenarios.body: Dream Of Ithaca, fresh after 59 days off and with a 3yo weight allowance, slots in behind the leader and the pair race clear before the final bend, leaving the hold-up horses with too much to do over this trip; the 10lb claimer aboard gives a slight tactical edge if the race develops into a two-horse battle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and runners arrive in a heap, making it a sprint finish from the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race compresses the field and hands an advantage to any horse who can quicken sharply; Alex The Great and Lady Lauren, though true hold-up types shuffled forward by the redistribution dynamic, would need the field to come back to them rather than finding their natural late position.

watchPoints.text: Gearing's Point — watch whether George Bass allows a fully uncontested lead or whether Dream Of Ithaca pushes up to track closely; if Gearing's Point gets a solo lead into the Brighton straight, it becomes very difficult to peg back in a small field.

Foinix — 45 days between runs and a hold-up style in a race with a modest, controlled pace means it must produce a career-best finishing effort to land from the back; watch the market moves for any stable confidence signal.

Dogged — nine-year-old with no recent Good-to-Firm win form who may find the uncontested pace too slow to generate the late momentum it relies on; if it is trapped wide or gets outpaced early in the straight, its chance evaporates quickly.

Lady Lauren and Alex The Great — both genuine hold-up types compressed into midfield by the field composition; watch whether either jockey (Owen Lewis, Myla Coppins) rides positively forward or tries to replicate a natural closing run that this small-field scenario may not create.

races.paceDynamic: Dion Baker is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him, William Carson can control the tempo from the front on the undulating Brighton 7f, dictating a sustainable gallop that plays directly to his stamina and course-proven consistency. Silver Trumpet and State Of Madness will press forward from their prominent draw, but neither is a true pace-setter, so Dion Baker should coast into a comfortable lead without being truly tested early. Dontspoilasale may also attempt to track up close, yet her form profile suggests she will settle just off the pace rather than challenge for the lead. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can travel in the slipstream of an uncontested leader, as the moderate, controlled tempo is unlikely to set up a decisive late burst for genuine hold-up horses; the field contains more hold-up types than can get to the rear, with Just Jump mapped forward despite being a natural closer who is unlikely to secure that position in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dion Baker Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Dion Baker secures the lead uncontested and Carson settles him into a rhythm, the race is run at a controlled pace that suits front-runners and prominent chasers.
scenarios.body: Dion Baker dictates from the front with no genuine rival to stretch him early, and his strong Brighton form (three wins in similar conditions) makes him extremely hard to peg back once he picks up turning for home; Silver Trumpet and State Of Madness, travelling just behind, are best placed to benefit if Dion Baker is caught late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Trumpet or State Of Madness travel smoothly just off Dion Baker and produce a sharper turn of foot in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In a moderate-tempo race a horse travelling comfortably just off the pace retains more energy for the finish, and Silver Trumpet's course win over this trip in good ground gives her tactical speed credentials; State Of Madness's placed form over 7f on good going also positions her to strike if the leader fades.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front runners tire badly in the closing stages, leaving room for a finisher.
scenarios.body: Serenity Dream has the most credible hold-up profile in this field with recent placed form on quick ground, and North View's patient style could see her pick up ground late if the race falls apart; however, the controlled pace scenario makes a true late sprint unlikely, and Just Jump's redistribution away from its natural role further reduces the probability of this shape materialising.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, No Clear Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Trumpet and Dontspoilasale both try to press Dion Baker early, creating a contested lead that scrambles the expected pace shape.
scenarios.body: A faster, pressured gallop could see Dion Baker weaken late and open the race up for those held up slightly wider, though this scenario requires multiple prominent horses to all try for the front simultaneously, which is unlikely given the disparity in their natural styles; Serenity Dream and North View would be the primary beneficiaries if the race becomes truly messy.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Silver Trumpet attempts to close on Dion Baker from the 2f pole — if she travels smoothly into second rounding the final bend she becomes the most dangerous horse in the race to the leader.

Monitor Dion Baker's early strides: if Carson elects to push forward aggressively to nullify any pressure from Silver Trumpet or Dontspoilasale, a faster-than-expected tempo could dramatically change the race shape and bring hold-up horses into contention.

Just Jump is racing out of her natural hold-up role and has been mapped to midfield — if she instinctively drops back to her true position she could be caught with too much ground to make up on a controlled-pace Brighton track, undermining her chances entirely.

State Of Madness returns from a 45-day break and her readiness is uncertain; watch her in the paddock and early in the race to see whether she travels with her usual fluency or shows signs of ring-rustiness that would confirm the layoff has blunted her sharpness.

Brighton's undulating track rewards horses that handle the downhill camber into the straight — Dion Baker's strong course record (multiple wins here) gives him a significant positional advantage that flat-track form alone does not capture.
